rule: Only this wave's own worktrees and temporary folders are removed, from the main repository, by exact path: git worktree remove --force <path> for a worktree, Remove-Item -LiteralPath for a folder or file that is not a worktree, never a wildcard. A worktree is removed with --force only after both checks pass: (a) every tracked change in it is byte-identical (LF-normalised) to the committed file it produced; (b) every untracked file is byte-identical to its copy in the main tree's run folder (cmp over git -c core.quotepath=off status --porcelain --untracked-files=all), or is a reproducible, non-acceptance output named here. --force covers nothing else. Directories left by earlier waves are not touched. A first PowerShell call that iterated over a variable list was refused by the tool because it read the protected parent D:\tmp as the target; it removed nothing, and each path was then removed by its own explicit command.
